doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Eldridge Morrison the chauffeur, principal Lane and Mrs. Hamlin
summary: Eldridge drove the principal; Johnson adds an aside about the glamorous Spanish teacher Mrs. Hamlin.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: And this is while you all were still in high school?

For the most part, yes. Eldridge was an interesting guy – very bright, very sharp, very intense, very much interested in music. He was the chauffeur, like a chauffeur for the principal of the school. That was his main gig, shall we say – chauffeuring for the principal.
You know, Lane lived right down the street from where you were on Indianapolis [Avenue], because we lived in that same block.
And Dr. Lane’s house was on the corner.

Uh huh. Yeah. The teacher [that] I remember that all the guys had their eyes on because she was such an attractive, stately, statuesque woman was Mrs. Hamlin, our Spanish teacher. She was a real looker, a real traffic stopper. All of the guys had their eyes on Mrs. Hamlin because she was just a gorgeous woman. Just an aside.
A happy memory that just flitted across.
